verdict: Avoid new pharma/API exposure in Baddi for now; lend only to CDMO-linked, export-order-backed units with verified raw-material pass-through, and decline margin-crushed generics/paracetamol players.
title: Baddi Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Baddi units convert imported API and intermediates into tablets, capsules and bulk drugs, and cash comes back only after a long conversion-and-collection cycle.** The plant buys raw material (much of India's API import basket is China-sourced, 65-70% of total API imports [11]), runs formulation or API lines, and sells to domestic formulators or export clients. Value sits in the customer relationship and regulatory approvals, not the building. **Working capital is the real business: receivables and inventory are heavy** — peer Concord ran working-capital intensity of 52% in FY2019, 47% in FY2020 and 48% in 7MFY2021 [10]. So when a proposal lands, check the receivable days and inventory holding against these peer levels; if the borrower's intensity is materially higher, ask why before sizing the limit.

## What has broken now
**Input costs have doubled and Baddi units are completing old orders at a loss.** Local reporting says crude-linked raw material prices have doubled, with paracetamol quoted at 500 per kg, and industrialists say they are honouring old orders at a loss [2]. That is a margin event, not a demand event, and it hits fixed-price contract manufacturers hardest. **The local economy is also running well behind India:** Himachal Pradesh GST collections are -22.8% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and electricity demand is -6.8% against India +9.5% [D]. Nationally, bank credit is +21.6% YoY while output is -2.1% [D] — money is being lent faster than goods are being made. So when a proposal lands, check whether the order book is at old fixed prices or re-priced; if the borrower cannot show a pass-through clause, ask for the customer-wise price revision history.

## Where the growth is
**Pursue CDMO and API capacity builders, not plain generic formulators.** Morepen Laboratories has begun groundbreaking for a new CDMO and API facility at its Baddi plant [3] — that is the borrower type to follow: contract-backed, capability-led capex. Peer results confirm the segment is paying: Aarti Pharmalabs reported record quarterly revenue of Rs. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% from 17.7% [4][6], and RPG Life Sciences is targeting 25% API growth with another acquisition within 12 months [5]. **Avoid units with no pricing power and no export or CDMO contract** — the loss-making old-order behaviour in [2] is exactly that profile. Note the local sources say little about Baddi-specific credit data; lean on first principles and these peers.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the balance sheet.** Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, monthly GST returns, and a quarterly raw-material price-versus-selling-price reconciliation. **Covenant on receivable days and inventory days at peer levels [10]**, and require a minimum pass-through clause on new orders. For capex borrowers like the CDMO type [3], tie disbursement to commissioning milestones and keep a DSRA. Collect from customer: current receivable days, inventory days, and the share of order book at fixed versus re-priced rates.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for old-order losses turning into receivable stretch.** If monthly GST turnover falls while limits stay drawn, cut exposure. If raw-material prices stay doubled [2] and the borrower's selling prices have not moved, treat it as a margin call, not a liquidity blip. If the state's GST and power numbers stay this far behind India [D], assume local demand is weak and price accordingly.
watch: Turnover falls two months running while drawing power stays full -> freeze enhancement, review limit
Input cost up with no price revision -> ask for pass-through proof, shift to LC-backed orders
Above peer 47-52% working-capital intensity [10] -> demand stock statement, reduce limit
Share of fixed-price old orders rising -> decline new exposure until re-priced
HP stays well behind India [D] -> tighten new-to-bank approvals in Baddi

news_why: Raw material doubled, old orders booked at a loss, HP GST and power well behind India.
